ios.desc:
AI writes the code. Your name is still on the PR.

GooseCode is the canvas in the middle — an infinite canvas where your coding agent draws what it built, your team collaborates in real time, and you steer what's next with concise visuals instead of walls of text.

Reading code is the new bottleneck. Tabs and jump-to-definition were built when code was read at the speed it was written — that broke the moment a model could write a thousand lines while you drink your coffee. GooseCode turns your codebase into easy to understand visuals — architecture, flows, and diffs drawn straight from the repo — with your notes, documentation, and references on the same canvas as the code they describe.

Your team works on the same board in real time: sketch over the agent's diagrams, annotate the code, and comment in place instead of in a thread. What you draw together stays — the whiteboard from Tuesday's call is still there next sprint, and a snapshot shares it with whoever missed it. The reasoning behind every decision lives on the canvas, next to the code it produced.

You don't learn GooseCode. Connect its MCP server to your coding agent and ask in plain language — the agent draws on the canvas, then reads it back, so you stop re-explaining your architecture every session.

Use GooseCode to:
- Debug complex issues visually
- See exactly what your agent touched before you sign off
- Review and steer agent work as a team
- Document a codebase with diagrams drawn from the real code
- Onboard new developers with a map, not a maze
- Run design sessions on a whiteboard that persists
- Share any canvas as a snapshot

Works alongside your existing IDE, with VS Code or Cursor extensions. Connect GitHub with OAuth, or use fine-grained access to limit GooseCode to only the repositories you choose.

quotes.text:
Modern software development tooling focuses on writing code. GooseCode is designed for visualizing code, understanding relationships and keeping documentation alongside real code.

Think Figma / Miro for software developers.

I build GooseCode because I constantly lose my flow while tabbing back and forward through the IDE, with a pen and paper to keep track on my desk.

GooseCode currently focus on reading and visualizing code, with IDE integration and writing on the horizon.
